newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel sees further cuts in social welfare in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Waigel sees further cuts in social welfare in 1997.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday that it was necessary to cut government spending on social welfare by another one billion marks next year to fill the widening budget gap.

Already finding it difficult to meet the strict fiscal criteria for entry into European economic and monetary union in 1999, the German government does not want an additional budget shortfall of three billion marks next to widen the deficit.
Commenting on a report in the mass daily Bild, Waigel told German radio that high unemployment was fuelling a steep rise in the labour office budget that had to be capped.
"The requirement would be around 13 billion marks next year. We cannot afford that. There must be further savings of around one billion marks in social welfare budgets," he said.
Waigel said the federal budget must be squuezed further next year to account for an additional shortfall in revenues of around three billion marks.
He wants to save one billion marks in the labour office budget and another two billion marks across the board.

Waigel complained that the Social Democrats (SPD), the main opposition in the lower house of parliament, were blocking passage of key savings legislation in the upper house, where the SPD have a majority.
